task_summary: Verify Ising-model pipeline, run falsification experiment, review sessions for paper

steps.title: Line-by-line code audit of the full pipeline
steps.description: On math-alderaan, read every script that produces a reported number end to end: model.py (coniii MCH Ising fit), main.py/main-wells.py, arbitration_many.py, arbitration_j_many.py, pk_j_analysis.py, peak_timing_analysis.py, peak_near_max_velocity.py, test_j_timing_vs_kinematics.py, test_collective_j_timing.py, build_decision_tree_dataset.py, run_decision_tree.py, simulate_neural_regimes.py, compare_sessions.py. For each, check: correct spin encoding (0/1 vs -1/+1), correct handling of NaN/missing kinematics bins, correct null-model definition used for the 'collective behavior' flag (Ising closer AND dist>0.1), correct alignment of J/H time series to kinematic time series (off-by-one bin risk), and whether thresholds (e.g. tol=0.02, dist>0.1) are justified or arbitrary. Cross-check each script's logic against the specific numeric claims already written in the per-folder READMEs and RESULTS_SUMMARY.md. Save findings, with exact file:line citations, as code_audit_findings.md.

steps.title: Raw-data spot-check recomputation (5-6 sessions)
steps.description: Pick 5-6 representative sessions spanning normal cases and the known outlier (220515), including at least one from each recording batch (fChR2/fChR5/fChR4/cChR1/DJC). Load the raw .mat spike files directly from /data001/projects/enserrog/AbigailData/energy_over_time/, independently re-derive (fresh code, not copy-pasted from the pipeline) N neurons, spike-bin matrix shape, mean firing rates, and pairwise correlations C_ij, and cross-check against the pipeline's cached intermediate outputs for the same sessions. Also independently recompute the P(K) empirical distribution and the 'Ising closer than independent' comparison from the cached h/J fits to confirm the reported r_ising/r_independent/collective-behavior flags are reproducible. Run as a single SLURM batch job (sbatch, not interactive shell) with adequate cores. Save verification_spotcheck.csv (per-session comparison of pipeline vs independently-recomputed values) and a short markdown write-up of any discrepancies found.

steps.title: Surrogate-null falsification experiment (core new experiment)
steps.description: Directly test the paper's central claim by assuming the method carries no real collective-activity information and trying to reject that null. For each session in the audit sample (extend to all sessions if the SLURM job finishes with time to spare), generate firing-rate-matched surrogate spike trains that destroy pairwise synchrony (independent-neuron shuffling across time bins, preserving each neuron's own rate profile) with 100-200 shuffle repeats. Refit the Ising model (coniii MCH) on each surrogate, recompute the P(K) Ising-vs-independent distance and the energy/J-coupling arbitration statistic, and build a null distribution of these effect sizes per session. Compare the real-data effect size against this null (empirical p-value) to determine whether the reported collective-behavior signal exceeds chance. Submit as a SLURM job parallelized across shuffles/sessions with multiprocessing/joblib and --cpus-per-task=16+ as the cluster guidance specifies. Produce a real-vs-null comparison figure (plain, no formatting polish yet) and a results table/write-up: surrogate_null_control_results.csv + writeup.md.

steps.title: Session-level diagnostics and outlier review
steps.description: Compile one master table across every session x stimulus condition (all ~21-24 sessions) pulling already-computed values from the results tree: N neurons, r_ising (pairwise and triplet), P(K) fit distance, collective-behavior flag, arbitration classification, J-coupling peak timing/lag classification. Identify outlier sessions beyond the already-known 220515 case (e.g. by z-scoring each metric across sessions), and check whether outliers correlate with recording batch, N neurons, or session length. Save session_diagnostics_table.csv and an outlier write-up with supporting plain diagnostic plots (unformatted, for internal review only).

steps.title: Run and document the decision-tree stage
steps.description: Execute build_decision_tree_dataset.py then run_decision_tree.py on math-alderaan (currently has zero narrative write-up per project memory -- only raw run outputs exist). Use proper train/test split or cross-validation, capture real accuracy/AUC and feature-importance numbers, and write a findings note (decision_tree_findings.md) covering what the tree does and does not support, to close the one clearly-identified documentation gap in the existing analysis.

steps.title: Capture the target figure-format spec (no regeneration yet)
steps.description: Document the exact convention already used in shared/results/comparisons/ (bold top-left panel labels like 'A1'/'B1', no in-plot legend, one companion .txt sidecar per figure holding the quantitative summary that becomes the caption) as figure_format_spec.md with a concrete example (fields, ordering, precision). This captures the target style for when figure regeneration is authorized later, per your instruction to hold off on editing figures until claims are verified.

steps.title: Compile the master verification + paper-prep report
steps.description: Write VERIFICATION_REPORT.md synthesizing all of the above: a methods section framing the Ising/Hamiltonian energy-decomposition approach as a general collective-activity detector (not Purkinje-cell-specific), the code-audit outcome, the raw-data spot-check outcome, the surrogate-null falsification result and what it does/doesn't prove about the method's unique ability to detect collective behavior beyond firing-rate/independent-neuron accounts, the session-outlier findings, the decision-tree findings, and an explicit, numbered list of remaining holes and open questions (generalizability evidence needed for non-cerebellar systems, any unresolved discrepancies from the audit, any session-level anomalies left unexplained) for you to weigh in on before figure work or manuscript drafting begins.

feasibility.rationale: The code, intermediate results, and raw .mat spike files are all reachable on the HPC cluster (64 CPU/512GB nodes, SLURM). The hardest new piece — a surrogate-null control that tests whether the Ising/P(K) collective-activity signal exceeds what chance-level firing-rate-matched shuffling produces — is a well-established statistical technique (comparable to jitter/shuffle controls in the Unitary-Events/SPADE literature) and is directly computable by re-running the existing fitting pipeline on shuffled spike trains many times per session.
